claims.claim_text: The indexed Sergeant Milton Felsen is the New York-born Lincoln Brigade veteran and OSS member documented by NPS and NYU.
claims.evidence_excerpt: two sergeants, Milton Felsen and Irving Goff
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS names Sergeant Milton Felsen as an OSS-trained former Spanish Civil War veteran, while NYU documents the same distinctive name, prewar history, OSS service, wound, and captivity.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the distinctive exact name, matching Sergeant rank, OSS service, Spanish Civil War history, wound, and prisoner-of-war chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources place Felsen's Spanish service before World War II and his OSS service by early 1943.
claims.match_notes: The adjacent serial-only row remains a separate ambiguous entity; this claim applies only to the row carrying the Sergeant rank.

claims.claim_text: Before OSS service, Felsen served with the Abraham Lincoln Battalion in Spain as a machine gunner and later an ambulance driver.
claims.evidence_excerpt: machine-gunner in the Abraham Lincoln Battalion
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NYU's finding aid says Felsen volunteered in May 1937, was wounded while serving as a machine gunner, and completed his Spanish service as an ambulance driver.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The institutional biography matches the Sergeant row through the distinctive name and the same Spanish-war and OSS chronology reported by NPS.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar military assignment; not shown to be immediately before OSS.
claims.match_notes: This foreign military service is not a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: In February 1941, Felsen was elected recording secretary of the Veterans of the Abraham Lincoln Brigade's New York Post.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The organization's March 1941 bulletin reports the New York Post's February 5 election and names Felsen as recording secretary.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The uncommon exact name and Lincoln Brigade history align with the NPS and NYU records for the indexed Sergeant.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded to early 1941, but not proven to be the immediate pre-OSS affiliation.
claims.match_notes: An elected institutional role is documented; paid employment is not.

claims.claim_text: Felsen attended the University of Iowa before volunteering in Spain.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NYU places Felsen at the University of Iowa before his May 1937 departure for the International Brigades.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The same institutional biography supplies the distinctive name and corroborated OSS and Spanish-war chronology.

claims.claim_text: The adjacent serial-only Milton Felsen row may represent the same veteran as the Sergeant row, but the accessible reviewed sources do not link its private identifier.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The index prints two adjacent same-name rows in the same box, one with a private identifier and the other with Sergeant rank; external sources establish the Sergeant but not the serial-only row.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Plausible same person from adjacency, exact name, and box, but no reviewed source connects the serial-only row's private identifier to the documented veteran.
claims.temporal_assessment: The unresolved identity prevents publication of pre-OSS affiliations for this row.
claims.match_notes: The row remains separate and requires personnel-file review; the private identifier is not published.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Captain Irving Goff is the Lincoln Brigade veteran later recruited into OSS service.
claims.evidence_excerpt: two sergeants, Milton Felsen and Irving Goff
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS traces Goff from Sergeant and Spanish-war veteran through OSS assignments, while a reputable obituary reports his recruitment and discharge as a captain.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the distinctive exact name, rank progression to Captain, Spanish Civil War history, and detailed OSS Mediterranean chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources establish prewar Spanish service, a 1941 veterans-organization role, and subsequent OSS service.
claims.match_notes: The index note also AS is preserved as printed and is not expanded without archival evidence.

claims.claim_text: Goff served as a guerrilla officer in the Lincoln Brigade during 1937-1938.
claims.evidence_excerpt: guerrilla captain in the Loyalist Lincoln Brigade
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A contemporary report reprinted by the brigade veterans' organization dates Goff's guerrilla service to 1937 and 1938; NPS independently identifies him as a Spanish Civil War veteran.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The unusual exact name and consistent guerrilla and OSS chronology support the match.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar foreign military assignment, not immediate to OSS.
claims.match_notes: The title Captain in Spain is not silently equated with the later U.S. Army Captain rank.

claims.claim_text: In early 1941, Goff served in the Veterans of the Abraham Lincoln Brigade's national office as National Executive Secretary and Secretary-Treasurer.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The March 1941 organizational bulletin repeatedly identifies Goff in the national office and prints correspondence addressed to him as secretary-treasurer.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact name, Lincoln Brigade history, and later OSS identity align across contemporary, official, and obituary sources.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded to early 1941; the reviewed sources do not prove a direct transition into OSS.
claims.match_notes: The role is an institutional affiliation; salary or employment status is not established.

claims.claim_text: Before going to Spain, Goff worked as an adagio dancer; the source does not name an employer or establish self-employment.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Lieutenant Goff was an adagio dancer
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A contemporary 1939 Harvard Crimson report identifies Goff's occupation before his Spanish service.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The exact name, Spanish guerrilla role, and officer designation align with the better-documented OSS veteran.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented before 1937, but not immediate to OSS.
claims.match_notes: No dance company, engagement, or employing organization is invented.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Colonel Paul H. Gale is highly likely to be the 1st Infantry Division staff officer whom Donovan recruited into OSS.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Captain Paul Gale, a staff officer
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS identifies a Captain Paul Gale on the 1st Division staff and explicitly states that Donovan later recruited him; the index supplies the middle initial and later Colonel rank.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the exact first and last name, compatible officer-rank progression, 1st Division chronology, and direct OSS recruitment.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official account places Gale with the division in July 1943 before Donovan's recruitment.
claims.match_notes: The middle initial appears in the index but not the NPS narrative; personnel-file review should confirm the link.

claims.claim_text: Gale's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the U.S. Army's 1st Infantry Division, where he was a Captain and staff officer.
claims.evidence_excerpt: whom Donovan later recruited for OSS
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS explicitly describes Gale as a 1st Division staff officer and says Donovan later recruited him for OSS.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence match to the indexed Colonel based on name, compatible rank progression, and recruitment chronology.
claims.match_notes: The military assignment is not a civilian employer; no reliable civilian predecessor was identified.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Lieutenant Colonel Serge Obolensky is the Russian-born New York hotel executive and National Guard officer documented in official OSS sources.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact distinctive name and rank appear in the index and a 1943 OSS mission-personnel memorandum; NPS supplies the matching biography and recruitment chronology.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by the distinctive exact name, exact Lieutenant Colonel rank, official mission document, and consistent NPS chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: NPS traces his prewar employment, National Guard service, and early-1942 entry into Donovan's organization.
claims.match_notes: The full private service number is not required for the public identity claim.

claims.claim_text: Obolensky's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the New York National Guard; after Pearl Harbor, Donovan obtained an Army commission for him.
claims.evidence_excerpt: joined the New York National Guard
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS reports that Obolensky rose from private to captain in the Guard, then approached Donovan, received an Army commission, and reported in early 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed within the same detailed official biography and by the matching 1943 OSS memorandum.
claims.match_notes: The National Guard role is a military assignment, not a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: In 1935, Obolensky began consulting and promotional work for New York's St. Regis Hotel.
claims.evidence_excerpt: consulting and promoting the renovated St. Regis Hotel
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS dates Obolensky's St. Regis appointment to 1935 and says it led him into the hotel business.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The employment appears within the confirmed official biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar employment; not proven to be the final civilian employer before National Guard service.
claims.match_notes: The historical hotel is named; no current owner or successor is substituted.

claims.claim_text: Obolensky worked in banking and real estate in New York during the 1920s; the reviewed source does not name employers.
claims.evidence_excerpt: Working in banking and real estate in New York
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS describes Obolensky's 1920s work by sector and location without identifying an employing organization.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The occupation appears within the confirmed official biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented prewar occupation, not immediate to OSS.
claims.match_notes: No bank or real-estate firm is inferred.

person_updates.identity_evidence: This serial-only Milton Felsen row is adjacent to a Sergeant row with the same name and box. The accessible sources establish the Sergeant's biography but do not connect the private identifier to him.
person_updates.next_action: Review both Box 231 files together and compare the private identifier, enlistment, rank, birth date, Spanish service, wound, and captivity records before any merge or affiliation transfer.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The indexed Sergeant Milton Felsen aligns with NPS's Sergeant and Spanish-war veteran and NYU's distinctive Milton Felsen biography, which documents Lincoln Battalion, OSS, wound, and prisoner-of-war service.
person_updates.next_action: Review both Box 231 files together to resolve the adjacent serial-only row, establish OSS entry chronology, and identify any civilian employer between Spanish service and OSS recruitment.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The distinctive indexed Captain Irving Goff aligns with NPS's Spanish-war veteran and OSS officer, a contemporary veterans bulletin, a 1939 occupation report, and a reputable obituary reporting OSS recruitment and discharge as captain.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 279 for the meaning of also AS, exact OSS entry date, any intervening civilian employer, and whether his 1941 veterans-organization office was paid.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The indexed Colonel Paul H. Gale aligns with NPS's Captain Paul Gale, 1st Infantry Division staff officer, based on the exact first and last name, compatible officer progression, Sicily chronology, and explicit later OSS recruitment.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 258 to confirm the middle initial against the 1st Division officer, establish the transfer date and OSS role, and identify any pre-Army civilian employer.

person_updates.identity_evidence: The exact distinctive name and Lieutenant Colonel rank appear in the NARA index and an August 1943 OSS mission-personnel memorandum; NPS supplies the matching New York employment, Guard, recruitment, training, and Sardinia chronology.
person_updates.next_action: Review Box 566 for the exact end of the St. Regis role, any later named hotel employer, National Guard unit and dates, Army commission, and OSS entry orders.
